claims.claim_text: The indexed P-5 Paul Baran is economist Paul Alexander Baran, who joined OSS under economist Edward S. Mason.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Baran joins the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), working under E.S. Mason
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Stanford's archival chronology aligns the exact name, civilian-to-Army status change, economics specialty, and 1942-1945 OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the uncommon exact name, P-5 civilian grade, profession, OSS employer, supervisor, and wartime chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Stanford explicitly dates his Brookings, OPA, OSS, Army, and bombing-survey sequence.
claims.match_notes: The P-5 index row likely reflects Baran's initial civilian phase before he was drafted and reassigned to OSS; Box 35 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Paul Baran's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Office of Price Administration.
claims.evidence_excerpt: After working briefly at the Office of Price Administration, Baran joins the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Stanford's finding aid expressly sequences the OPA assignment immediately before OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the same institutional chronology identifies Baran by full name, profession, supervisor, and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: OPA is a government assignment, not a civilian private employer.

claims.claim_text: From 1941 to 1942, Paul Baran held a Brookings Institution research fellowship on price-control problems.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Baran accepts research fellowship working on problems of price controls at the Brookings Institution
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Stanford chronology documents the institution, role, subject, and dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; this entry belongs to the same detailed Paul Alexander Baran chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation before the brief OPA interval and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The fellowship is not labeled salaried employment; Box 35 may clarify pay and appointment status.

claims.claim_text: From 1935 to 1938, Paul Baran worked for his uncles' timber business and became its London representative.
claims.evidence_excerpt: works for his uncles' timber business in Vilna, and eventually moves to London as the company's representative
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Stanford documents the unnamed family business, locations, role, and years.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the evidence is part of the same institutional biographical chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, not the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: No organization name is invented from the generic family-business description.

claims.claim_text: The initials-only indexed G. E. Buxton is Gonzalo Edward "Ned" Buxton Jr., first assistant director of OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact initials and surname, Brown and Rhode Island background, colonel title, and OSS assistant-director role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; an official OSS memorandum and reputable Rhode Island biography supply a distinctive full name and senior role.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography sequences private-sector leadership, 1941 COI recruitment, and OSS service through June 1945.
claims.match_notes: The unranked Box 98 index row is preserved. His retired Army colonel title is not used to turn the indexed row into a wartime commissioned-officer classification.

claims.claim_text: G. Edward Buxton's probable immediate pre-COI affiliation was the presidency of B. B. & R. Knight Company.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In 1926, he rose to the presidency of the giant textile firm of BB&R Knight Company
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Bar Journal says he held the textile presidency through the 1930s, then was recruited into the new civilian White House unit.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; full name, Rhode Island career, military title, and senior OSS office align with the official memorandum.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate: the sequence is strong but a possible 1939-1941 interval remains unaccounted for.
claims.match_notes: Displayed with a qualification. Box 98 is needed to confirm the exact recruitment date and any intervening work.

claims.claim_text: B. B. & R. Knight Company is the last identified civilian employer before Buxton's COI and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Rhode Island Bar biography presents no later private employer between the textile presidency and federal recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence identity; the employment sequence is supported by one reputable biographical source.
claims.temporal_assessment: Medium confidence because the exact end date and any 1939-1941 activity require the personnel file.
claims.match_notes: This is the last identified employer, not an assertion that no intervening affiliation existed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel James R. Forgan is investment banker James Russell "Russ" Forgan, later deputy OSS chief in Europe.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He was ably supported by his deputy, Col. Russell Forgan.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Exact surname and initials, colonel rank, Russell name, New York banking career, and senior OSS European role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the unusual name, rank, finance career, and official OSS role provide several corroborating identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: Contemporary reporting documents his prewar banking career; official CIA history documents the 1944 OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The full indexed service number remains private. Box 243 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Glore, Forgan & Co. is James Russell Forgan's last identified civilian employer before Army and OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: the two senior partners have been Charles Foster Glore and James Russell Forgan
claims.evidence_paraphrase: TIME identifies Forgan as senior partner and Manhattan-office head in 1937; official CIA sources establish his later OSS role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence identity; the employment-to-service transition is not directly dated.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, but the exact departure date and any intervening assignment remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The claim is phrased as last identified employer, not an unqualified immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Everette H. Hunt Jr. is Brown graduate and OSS lieutenant Everette Howard Hunt Jr.
claims.evidence_excerpt: A cryptic note in Everette Howard Hunt Jr.'s alumni file at Brown
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact first name, surname, suffix and middle initial align with Brown, NPS, and CIA records of OSS and China service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the unusual full name, suffix, Brown education, lieutenant status, China theater, and OSS affiliation align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Brown dates graduation and military entry; NPS places the 27-year-old lieutenant in China as a new OSS recruit.
claims.match_notes: The full index number remains private. Box 357 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: The best-supported immediate pathway into Hunt's OSS assignment is U.S. military service as a lieutenant.
claims.evidence_excerpt: a 27-year-old lieutenant from upstate New York, a Brown University graduate
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Brown says Hunt entered military service after graduation; NPS describes him as a lieutenant and brand-new OSS recruit in China.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence identity; exact military component and transfer orders remain unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military assignment, qualified because the precise Navy-Army-OSS sequence is not stated in one authoritative source.
claims.match_notes: No civilian employer is substituted for the documented military pathway.

claims.claim_text: Hunt was a Brown University student before entering military service; Brown is not classified as his employer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: After graduating from Brown, he signed up with the military
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Brown's alumni article explicitly sequences graduation and military entry.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the institutional alumni file uses his full name and later OSS career.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student status ending in 1940.
claims.match_notes: No reliable civilian employer before military service has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed CPC-2 Shaw Livermore Jr. is best matched to the future historian born in 1926 and educated at Mercersburg and Harvard.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Shaw was born on December 6, 1926 in Cambridge, MA, the son of Evelyn and Shaw Livermore.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact rare name and suffix, father's name, age, Mercersburg chronology, and 1944 Harvard transition align with the civilian-grade index entry.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence but not confirmed; the personnel file is needed because no independent source reviewed explicitly mentions his OSS work.
claims.temporal_assessment: Institutional and obituary sources place the younger Shaw in school throughout the OSS period.
claims.match_notes: The exact rare Jr. name and CPC-2 civilian grade make another namesake unlikely, but Box 457 remains the direct confirmation source.

claims.claim_text: The current evidence documents Shaw Livermore Jr. as a Mercersburg Academy student during the early OSS years.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Shaw's boy entered Mercersburg Academy this last fall
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A February 1943 Dartmouth class note dates his entry; his obituary confirms Mercersburg before Harvard.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence identity; exact school-to-OSS chronology remains unverified.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented wartime student status, but not established as the immediate predecessor to his CPC-2 appointment.
claims.match_notes: No employer is inferred. Box 457 is required to date the appointment and determine whether school enrollment overlapped OSS work.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact Paul Baran name, P-5 civilian grade, economics work, explicit OPA-to-OSS chronology, E. S. Mason supervision, and later Army technical-sergeant status align in Stanford's finding aid.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 35 for the exact OPA and OSS appointment dates, P-5 duties, draft and reassignment orders, and whether the Brookings fellowship was salaried employment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The initials-only G. E. Buxton row aligns with official G. Edward Buxton assistant-director records and a reputable biography of Gonzalo Edward Buxton Jr.'s Rhode Island, textile, colonel, COI, and OSS career.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 98 for Buxton's recruitment papers, exact B. B. & R. Knight departure date, 1939-1941 activities, appointment status, and any intervening organization.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The James R. Forgan index name and colonel rank align with J. Russell Forgan, a prewar Glore, Forgan senior partner and official CIA-documented deputy OSS chief in Europe.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 243 and Army orders for the exact departure from Glore, Forgan, entry onto active military duty, and transfer or assignment to OSS.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact Everette H. Hunt Jr. index form aligns with Brown, NPS, CIA, and NARA evidence for Everette Howard Hunt Jr., a Brown graduate, lieutenant, China-based OSS recruit, writer, and war correspondent.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 357 and the September 7, 1944 biographic profile to establish the exact Navy, writing, Army, and OSS sequence. No reliable civilian employer before military service has yet been identified.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The rare exact Shaw Livermore Jr. name, CPC-2 civilian grade, 1926 birth, father also named Shaw, Mercersburg attendance beginning in 1942, and 1944 Harvard transition align.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 457 to confirm the identity directly, date the CPC-2 appointment, identify the OSS office and duties, and determine whether Mercersburg or Harvard enrollment immediately preceded or overlapped service.

research_attempts.query_text: "Paul Baran" OSS; "Paul Alexander Baran" Office of Price Administration; Brookings 1941; NARA index, CIA Reading Room, Stanford archive, obituary, scholarly biography, and institutional checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Searches initially returned the unrelated computer-network engineer Paul Baran; Wikipedia and derivative biographies were discovery-only; no CIA exact-name result improved on Stanford's archival chronology.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the identity, explicit OPA-to-OSS transition, Brookings fellowship, and earlier family timber employment without converting the fellowship into an employer claim.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 35 for the exact appointment, draft, reassignment, and fellowship pay records.

research_attempts.query_text: "G E Buxton" OSS; "Gonzalo Edward Buxton" employer 1940; B. B. & R. Knight; NARA index, CIA Reading Room, Brown, Rhode Island Bar, Providence Journal, obituary, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and military-wiki pages were discovery-only; search snippets from a blocked newspaper could not serve as final evidence; later board service did not answer the pre-COI question.
research_attempts.research_notes: Resolved the initials at high confidence and identified B. B. & R. Knight as the probable immediate and last identified civilian employer, visibly qualified for the 1939-1941 gap.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 98 and relevant company records for exact departure and recruitment dates.

research_attempts.query_text: "James R Forgan" OSS Colonel; "James Russell Forgan" banker; Glore Forgan; NARA index, CIA Reading Room, NPS, FRUS, TIME, Hoover finding-aid, obituary, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Conspiracy sites, genealogy pages, modern derivative biographies, and the younger James Russell Forgan were rejected; postwar Glore Forgan letterhead alone did not prove wartime continuity.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the identity and senior OSS role. Glore, Forgan is published only as the last identified prewar employer at medium temporal confidence.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 243, Army orders, and the Russell Forgan papers for the exact business-to-service transition.

research_attempts.query_text: "Everette Howard Hunt Jr" OSS; E. Howard Hunt Brown 1940; Navy Army China; NARA index and JFK releases, CIA Reading Room, NPS, Brown alumni file, newspaper obituary, occupation, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia, commercial biography pages, and unsourced assassination material were discovery-only or irrelevant; postwar CIA and Watergate material was not used to infer a pre-OSS employer.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the identity, Brown student status, and a qualified military pathway into OSS. No civilian employer before military service was established.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 357 and the 1944 biographic profile for the exact Navy, civilian writing, Army, and OSS sequence.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar faculty sources did not answer the wartime question; Wikidata and Goodreads were discovery-only; searches found no CIA exact-name result or direct independent OSS reference.
